scam.title: Protect yourself from scams
scam.lead: People run scams in the name of the lottery. Know the official fee and check every step yourself.
scam.banner: Registering for the lottery has an official fee of just one dollar ($1), set by the US State Department. Any extra money is the office's service charge.

facts.1: You can register yourself on the official site that the US State Department announces.
facts.2: If you use an office, make sure it registers on the official site only, and that you personally keep the confirmation number.
facts.3: Nobody can guarantee a win or raise your chances.
facts.4: You check the result yourself, only on the official Entrant Status Check. No email or message tells you that you won.
facts.5: Copycat sites look official. Make sure the address ends in .gov, and beware of anyone who asks for money to "win".

signs.1: Asks for money to "guarantee" a win or raise your chances.
signs.2: Tells you that you won by message, email or phone.
signs.3: Asks for a money transfer, card details or your passport before you check the official site.
signs.4: The address does not end in .gov, or the tone is urgent and threatening.

scam.fee: Registering for the lottery has an official fee of just one dollar ($1), set by the US State Department. Do not let anyone take more than that as the government fee; any extra money is the office's service charge.

guide.title: How do I find the price of food?
guide.lead: We will not give you a number. We show you where to see it yourself, in the city you plan to live in.
guide.step1: Open a supermarket site from the links below and pick a store in your intended city.
guide.step2: Build a one-week basket of what you actually buy and read the total.
guide.step3: Multiply by 4 and type the number into the calculator. Repeat now and then; prices change.
guide.note: These are external sites. We do not set prices and are not responsible for them.
guide.backToCalculator: Type the number into the calculator
guide.titleFor: How do I find the price of “{item}”?
guide.genericLead: We will not give you a number. We show you where to look, and you type the number into the calculator.
guide.genericStep1: Open the links below and look for the current fee or price.
guide.genericStep2: Type the number as you find it. Mind the currency, and whether it is one-off or monthly.
guide.genericStep3: Go back to the calculator and type the number. Check it now and then; prices and fees change.

guideHealth.title: How do I find the price of health insurance?
guideHealth.lead: We will not give you a number. The price depends on the state, your age, household size and income, and you see it yourself on the official US government site.
guideHealth.step1: Open HealthCare.gov, enter the ZIP code of your intended city, and your household members and ages.
guideHealth.step2: Browse the plans and the monthly premium of each plan.
guideHealth.step3: Type the monthly premium into the calculator. If you have children, include them in the household size so the premium covers them.
guideHealth.state: Some states run their own marketplace; HealthCare.gov sends you there automatically. We do not set prices.
guideHealth.subsidyWarning: HealthCare.gov may offer you a subsidy on the premium based on your income. As a new immigrant, do not take this subsidy; work out the full price without it.

itemIncludes.entryPhotos: one photo for each person on the entry: you, your spouse and the children

itemIncludes.familyPassports: the spouse's passport and each child's, not yours
itemIncludes.medicalExam: the examination, X-ray, blood test and vaccinations
itemIncludes.translation: a certified translator's fee and any stamp or attestation on documents
itemIncludes.civilCertificates: getting new originals: birth, marriage, degree and transcript
itemIncludes.militaryCertificate: the fee to get the military status or exemption certificate
itemIncludes.visaPhotos: the printed photos each person brings to the interview, separate from the entry photos
itemIncludes.interviewTravel: transport, a night's stay and meals around the interview, if you live outside Cairo
itemIncludes.passportCourier: the courier's fee for sending the passport back after the interview, if there is one
itemIncludes.otherPaperwork: any paperwork or fee before travel that has no box above
itemIncludes.travelInsurance: trip and medical cover for the first weeks, before your health insurance starts
itemIncludes.temporaryStay: a hotel or a furnished short stay until you get your flat
itemIncludes.applicationFees: the fee to apply and for the background and credit check
itemIncludes.securityDeposit: the sum the landlord holds until you hand the flat back. Not health or car insurance
itemIncludes.furniture: beds, a sofa, a table, a TV and any large appliances
itemIncludes.winterClothes: coats, boots and warm clothes, for each person
itemIncludes.householdBasics: kitchen items, bed linen and blankets, cleaning and bathroom supplies. Food is not here: it is in the monthly costs
itemIncludes.utilityDeposits: the sum companies hold before they start the service, not the monthly bill
itemIncludes.phoneLine: a SIM and activating the line, for each adult. The monthly plan is in the monthly costs
itemIncludes.licenseTests: test fees and getting the licence
itemIncludes.carPurchase: the price of the car only. Insurance and registration have their own boxes
itemIncludes.carInsuranceStart: the first insurance payment before you drive
itemIncludes.carRegistration: registration, plates and title transfer fees
itemIncludes.healthInsuranceStart: the first month's premium, before the monthly costs start
itemIncludes.childcareStart: enrolment and the first payment. The monthly cost is in the monthly costs
itemIncludes.otherMoving: any moving cost that has no box above
itemIncludes.rent: the month's rent only. Power and water have their own box
itemIncludes.food: groceries, supermarket and home cooking, for each person
itemIncludes.healthInsurance: the monthly premium once the insurance has started
itemIncludes.otherMonthly: any monthly cost that has no box above
itemIncludes.familyAbroadMonthly: rent, food and any cost of the family at home during this time
itemIncludes.quickPaperwork: registration, medical, documents and every fee up to the green card
itemIncludes.quickHousing: temporary stay, deposit, first rent, furniture and home supplies
itemIncludes.quickMonthly: rent, utilities, food, transport and health insurance for one month
